questions.question: A car left 4 hours later than the scheduled time but in order to reach its destination 480 km away in time, it had to increase its usual speed by 10 km/hr. What is the usual speed of the car?
questions.solution:
**Detailed solution:-**

Let the usual speed of the car be ‘x’ km/hr.

Time is taken to cover 480 km = Distance/Speed = 480/x hrs.

But, when the car left 4 hours left, the Speed of the car = (x + 10) km/hr.

⇒ Time taken = Distance/Speed = 480/(x + 10)

⇒ (480/x) - 4 = 480/(x + 10)

⇒ (480- 4x)/x = 480/(x + 10)

⇒ (480 - 4x)(x + 10) = 480x

⇒ 480x + 4800 - 4x² - 40x = 480x

 

⇒ 4x² + 40x - 4800 = 0 

⇒ x² + 10x - 1200 = 0 

⇒ x2 + 40x - 30x - 1200 = 0

⇒ x(x + 40) - 30(x + 40) = 0

⇒ (x + 40)(x - 30) = 0

⇒ x = -40, 30 

∵ Speed cannot be negative 

**∴ The required answer is __30__. 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**Distance = (X × Y)/(X - Y) [time difference]

⇒ [x × (x + 10)/10] × 4 = 480

⇒ x(x + 10) = 1200

⇒ x × (x + 10) = 30 × 40

⇒ x = 30 km/hr

questions.question: The average speed of a car is 1500 metres/minute. A sprinter covers 200 metres in 30 seconds. What is the difference in the speed of car and the speed of sprinter?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed of car in m/s = 1500 ÷ 60 = 25 m/s

Speed of sprinter in m/s = 200 ÷ 30 = 20/3 m/s

Difference in speed = 25 − 20/3 = (75 − 20) ÷ 3 = 55/3 m/s

**∴ The correct answer is 55/3 m/s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of car = 1500 metres/minute

Distance covered by sprinter = 200 metres

Time taken by sprinter = 30 seconds

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

1 minute = 60 seconds

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f8d56f077e88100fe2ac528eaedd8eaa24b5b3745e5b87250a992497cabf3c8c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Speed of car = 1500 metres ÷ 60 seconds

⇒ Speed of car = 25 m/s

⇒ Speed of sprinter = 200 metres ÷ 30 seconds

⇒ Speed of sprinter = 20/3 m/s

⇒ Difference in speed = Speed of car − Speed of sprinter

⇒ Difference = 25 − 20/3

⇒ Difference = (75 − 20) ÷ 3

⇒ Difference = 55/3 m/s

**∴ The correct answer is 55/3 m/s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply the speed by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

Average Speed

When traveling equal distances at varying speeds S₁ and S₂, the formula applied is: Average Speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

Relative Speed

If two bodies move in the same direction, relative speed = |S₁ − S₂|. If they move in opposite directions, relative speed = S₁ + S₂.

questions.question: Sunil drove for 2 hours at a rate of 50 miles per hour and for 3 hours at 60 miles per hour. What was his average speed for the whole journey?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Sunil drove 2 hours at rate of 50 miles per hours

Sunil drove 3 hours at rate of 60 miles per hours

**Concept:**

Average speed={Total distanceover Total time}

**Formula used:**

S={Dover T} Where, S = Speed, D = Distance, and T = Time

**Calculation:**

Let the average speed of the Sunil be S

The distance travel by Sunil in first travel = 2 × 50 = 100 miles

The distance traveled by Sunil in second travel = 3 × 60 = 180 miles

The total time = 2 + 3 = 5

The average speed S = {280over5}=56 miles per hours

**∴ The required result will be 56 miles per hours.**

questions.question: A speeding car traveling at 40 km/hr decides to slow down to 30 km/hr after covering half the distance. What is the average speed?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Car speed = 40 km/hr

Car's speed after slowing down = 30 km/hr

**Formula used:**

Average speed = Total distance/total time

**Calculation**

Let the total distance be 2x km

Time is taken to cover half the distance at 40 km/hr = x / 40 hr

Time is taken to cover rest half distance at 30 km/hr = x / 30 hr

Total time taken = x / 40 + x / 30

⇒ (3x + 4x) / 120

⇒ 7x / 120

Average speed = 2x / (7x / 120)

⇒ 240/7 km/hr

**∴ The average speed is 240/7 km/hr.**

questions.question: Ravi goes to college from his village at the speed of 5km/h and returns at the speed of 4km/h. If he takes 9 hours in all, find the distance (in km) between the village and the college.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed while going to college = 5 km/h.

Speed while returning = 4 km/h.

Total time taken = 9 hours.

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time.

For combined trips with different speeds, use the relationship between distance, speed, and time to set up an equation.

**Calculation:**

Let the distance between the village and the college be d kilometers.

Time taken to go to college = d / 5 hours.

Time taken to return = d / 4 hours.

Total time for both trips = Time to go + Time to return = 9 hours.

Setting up the equation:

(d / 5) + (d / 4) = 9

To solve for d, find a common denominator and solve the equation:

(4d + 5d) / 20 = 9

9d = 180

d = 180 / 9

d = 20 kilometers.

**Therefore, the distance between the village and the college is 20 kilometers.**
